_comment: Continues the az_15gb run on a Colab CPU runtime. Same network, same encoder, same search - only the batch sizes shrink to fit two vCPUs. Point it at the SAME --output directory as the GPU run and it picks up latest.pt; switching back to GPU later just means running the GPU config again.
_device: Forced, not autodetected. A CPU runtime has no CUDA so this changes nothing there, but it makes an accidental run on a GPU session impossible to mistake for the real thing.
_total_steps: 500 * 160 from colab_az_gumbel.json. The cosine schedule must keep the GPU run's horizon, otherwise resuming here would restart the decay under a different curve.
_steps: A 128x10 optimiser step costs ~4-6 s on two vCPUs, so 8 steps is already a third of the iteration. Self-play is the useful work here; training just keeps the net moving.
_save_every: latest.pt is ~150 MB. Iterations here are minutes, so saving every one would write over a gigabyte an hour to Drive; 10 caps the redone work at one iteration's worth.
_gate_every: Measured on this run: 21 s per game on two vCPUs, so one gate is 64 games = 23 min. Every 100 iterations that is 16% of wall clock, the same share the old every-50 setting cost with half as many games.
_gate_threshold: 16 games at 0.55 needed 9/16, which an evenly-matched candidate reaches 40% of the time - and two candidates are gated (live and ema) with the better one taken, so ~64% of gates promoted noise. Generations 9 and 10 both passed on 0.625/0.750 and 0.625/0.562, which is inside that band. 32 games at 0.65 needs 21/32: 5.5% false per candidate, ~11% for the pair, while still catching a genuinely 65%-strong net about half the time.
